title: Execute Private DR game day + write-up and follow-up action plan
creator: Rafael Mendes
description:
Goal
- Run a realistic disaster recovery (DR) game day for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem assumptions), validate backup/restore runbooks + automation, and produce an actionable follow-up plan.

Why
- Enterprise prospects (FinBank, MedData) are explicitly asking for evidence of repeatable DR procedures and RPO/RTO attainment. This game day is the internal bar for whether we can confidently claim “supported + documented + repeatable” recovery.

Scope for this game day
- Primary: Control-plane restore into a clean Kubernetes cluster using the new installer workflows (backup create / restore apply) + documented runbooks.
- Secondary: Validate observability and on-call readiness (dashboards/alerts, failure modes, escalation criteria).
- Out of scope: Full etcd cluster restore as the primary path (covered by infra runbook as last resort), and data-plane “stateful” restoration (data-plane should be stateless + redeployable; ensure config required for deterministic redeploy is captured).

Scenario (selected)
- “Cluster corruption / control-plane loss” in single-region VPC deployment.
- Constraints: no outbound internet during restore steps except to the configured backup storage endpoint (simulate restricted egress posture). Simulate IAM least-privilege role usage.

Participants (roles)
- Incident commander: Rafael Mendes
- Ops lead / executor: Sean Gallagher
- Control plane engineering support: Ethan Park / Benji Okafor
- Observability: Sergio Costa
- Security/crypto reviewer (observer): Hanae Suzuki
- PM/notes: Talia Benson

Pre-reads / artifacts
- Game day plan: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/game-days/private-dr-gameday-plan.json
- Prior rehearsal notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/dr-gameday-notes-2025-02-14.json
- Restore validation test plan: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/restore-validation-test-plan.json

Success criteria
- Execute restore end-to-end with runbooks only (no tribal knowledge), capture timestamps for RTO.
- Demonstrate we can meet target RPO (last successful backup age within target) and can validate integrity.
- Produce a write-up with: timeline, what broke, root causes, mitigations/workarounds, and a prioritized action plan (owners + deadlines).

Deliverables
- Confluence/Drive write-up link in this ticket.
- List of follow-up Linear issues (existing or newly filed), tagged and prioritized.

Notes
- Expectation is not “perfect run”; expectation is “we learn, capture gaps, and turn into concrete hardening work.”
acceptance_criteria: 1) Game day executed with recorded timeline (start/end + key steps). 2) RTO/RPO measured and compared to target for the chosen archetype. 3) Write-up published with clear findings and action items. 4) Follow-up tasks filed/linked with owners and priorities. 5) On-call escalation guidance updated (what pages, what doesn’t, and during which environments).
worklog:
2025-02-06: Finalized scenario choice (single-region VPC, cluster corruption) and attendee list. Confirmed restricted-egress simulation approach with Infra.
2025-02-10: Dry-run of runbook steps in staging; identified missing prerequisite checks (CRDs/Helm state) and added annotations for game day.
2025-02-14: Executed game day in staging environment (private-dr-stg-02). Captured full timeline, failure points, and recovery path.
2025-02-17: Published write-up + action plan; filed follow-up issues; updated paging recommendations for restore drills.
2025-02-18: Final review with Neha (reliability sponsor) and Vivek (product owner) on commitments vs gaps.
results_summary:
Outcome: Partial success with two major gaps.
- We successfully restored control-plane state into a clean cluster and regained API availability.
- We did NOT achieve the aspirational RTO target due to (a) missing CRD/ordering issues during restore and (b) confusion around backup artifact selection + verification output.

Measured times (staging, single-region VPC archetype)
- Time to identify latest valid backup artifact: 18m (too high; tooling/UX gap)
- Time from “restore apply start” to “control plane healthy”: 1h 42m (goal was < 60m for this archetype)
- Time to complete validation checklist (routing policies + tenant config): +31m

RPO check
- Last successful scheduled backup was within target window for the drill (backup age 45m at drill start). Integrity verification succeeded once the correct artifact was selected.

Key learnings
- Restore must be deterministic and “boring.” Any manual CRD/ordering work breaks the promise of repeatability.
- Observability needs a single “DR readiness” view: last_backup_success_ts, last_restore_drill_ts, and drill outcome with a link to logs/report.

Write-up
- Detailed notes: sources/google_drive/shared_drives/engineering/site-reliability-engineering/dr-gameday-notes-2025-02-14.json (linked in internal channels; add to customer-ready narrative later via docs).
follow_up_action_plan:
P0 (this week)
- Fix restore ordering to ensure required CRDs exist before applying dependent resources; enforce pre-flight detection with actionable error output. Owner: Benji Okafor. Link: SUP-18477 context + ENG restore workflow work.
- Improve backup artifact selection UX: add ‘latest valid backup’ resolver + explicit integrity/compatibility summary before restore proceeds. Owner: Michael Nguyen. (File/track under ENG-9830 + ENG-9822 follow-up.)
- Ensure restore validation emits a single machine-readable report (JSON + human summary) with pass/fail gates and pointers to failing checks. Owner: Sean Gallagher. (Follow-up on ENG-9822/PR-489 style output.)

P1 (next 2–3 weeks)
- Observability: dashboard tiles + alerts for last_success_ts, duration, bytes, drill status; tune paging to avoid noise in non-prod. Owner: Sergio Costa. Dependency: ENG-9826 / observability-pack PR-94.
- Add explicit runbook section: ‘When to use etcd snapshot restore vs application restore’ with decision tree + caveats. Owner: Miles Thornton + Kira Thompson. Reference: sources/confluence/eng-infra/runbooks/restore-k8s-cluster-from-etcd-snapshot.json.
- Release gating: require at least one successful automated restore drill in staging prior to cutting the Private release. Owner: Sahana Iyer + Connor O’Brien. Dependency: ENG-9827.

P2 (hardening)
- NFS backend performance guardrails and timeouts for slow storage; document recommended defaults. Owner: Bruno Silva. Reference: eng-infra thread on NFS tuning.
- Air-gapped drill variant (offline artifact import + signature verification) scheduled as a separate game day. Owner: Fatima Noor + Connor O’Brien. Dependency: ENG-9829.

comments: 2025-02-06 (Rafael Mendes): Locking Feb 14th as the drill date. We’ll run the single-region VPC scenario first; on-prem/air-gapped variant will be a separate drill once offline bundle/signing is ready (ENG-9829).

2025-02-10 (Sean Gallagher): Dry run found an easy-to-miss prerequisite: restore assumes CRDs present before applying manifests from backup. We need restore apply to either (a) install CRDs from the release bundle or (b) fail with a targeted message that points to the exact missing CRD + required chart/version.

2025-02-14 (Talia Benson): Timekeeping + notes captured live. Biggest slowdown: determining which artifact was ‘good’ (latest vs latest completed vs latest uploaded). Suggest adding a resolver command: `backup list --latest-valid` + `backup inspect`.

2025-02-14 (Ethan Park): The restore path is close, but we’re still relying on engineer intuition for ordering. We should encode ordering in the installer and treat manual kubectl edits as a failure in the runbook (unless explicitly called out as break-glass).

2025-02-17 (Sergio Costa): Metrics gaps noted: we can see CronJob success/fail but not ‘restore drill outcome’ in a standardized way. I’ll align with PR-94 structure and add a drill outcome metric + label dimensions (env, archetype, version).

2025-02-18 (Neha Kapoor): For external commitments, we should be careful to claim ‘supported DR runbook with validated RTO’ only after we hit <60m in at least 2 consecutive drills and have a gated release check. Please track as release criteria with Release Eng.
